history.period: Modern - idol enshrined in a new temple in 1937 (per Wikipedia and multiple travel sources)
history.summary: The 'Maa Bhairavi Temple' row best matches the Siddha Bhairavi Temple at Mantridi village, Ganjam district, Odisha - a well-known Shakti shrine. The presiding idol of Goddess Bhairavi is carved in crude fashion with one leg and four hands; legend says a farmer unearthed it while ploughing, and it was enshrined in the newly built temple in 1937 (this dating and the ploughing legend repeat consistently across sources). The complex is unusual for housing 108 sub-shrines dedicated to gods from Kashmir to Kanyakumari (12 Jyotirlingas, Dashavatara, Vaishno Devi, Venkateswara, Ranganatha, Meenakshi, Badrinath) plus a large Jagannath shrine; belief holds that Bhairavi will accompany Kalki at the end of Kali Yuga to restore dharma. Traditionally worshipped by sailors and fishermen before voyages. CSV corrections: town 'Berhampur' corrected to Mantridi - the temple is on National Highway 16 about 18 km from Berhampur, not in the city; district Ganjam and state Odisha are correct. Coordinates are published GPS coordinates (19.18696, 84.76919) for the temple. Opening hours 6:00 AM-6:00 PM are from a location listing (verify).
